evidence_frontier.status: Alpha5 remains active. Exp021 found a 4,278-parameter w8 compression candidate at exactly 10 fewer Q.ANT correct predictions out of 1000 than the Alpha5 control; the preregistered floating-point gate recorded retain_alpha5.

analysis: Observation: Exp021 evaluated a w8‑compressed Alpha5 (4278 parameters) and observed 887 aggregate correct predictions versus 897 for the full Alpha5 on ECG200 using 10 random seeds (1000 total predictions). The decision was to retain Alpha5 because the performance drop matched the preregistered floating‑point gate. Hypothesis: The same integer‑count performance gap (≤10 fewer correct predictions) will be reproducible when the experiment is repeated with an independent set of random seeds, confirming that the w8 compression boundary is stable under integer‑count gating.
hypothesis: When the w8‑compressed Alpha5 (local_width = 8, 4,278 parameters) is evaluated on ECG200 with a fresh, preregistered seed set, its aggregate Q.ANT correct count will not fall more than 10 below the full Alpha5 control (i.e., ≥ 887 correct out of 1000).

proposal.title: Confirmation of w8 Compression Boundary on ECG200 with Integer‑Count Gating
proposal.research_question: Does the w8‑compressed Alpha5 reliably reproduce the ≤10‑prediction performance gap relative to full Alpha5 on ECG200 when evaluated with an independent seed set and integer‑count gating?
proposal.rationale: Exp021 demonstrated a borderline performance drop for the w8 candidate using floating‑point gates. To solidify the compression boundary as a reproducible design rule, a confirmation experiment using integer‑count gating (aggregate correct predictions) is required. This avoids reinterpretation of Exp021 while providing a statistically clear success metric.

procedure: Train the full Alpha5 baseline on ECG200 using 10 independent random seeds (seed set A).
Compress the trained Alpha5 to the w8 configuration (local_width = 8, 4,278 parameters) without altering frequency basis or readout rule.
Train the w8‑compressed model on the same training data using the same 10 seeds (seed set B, independent from set A).
Evaluate both models on the ECG200 test set for each seed, recording per‑seed correct counts.
Sum correct predictions across the 10 seeds (1000 total predictions) for each model.
Apply the integer‑count gating: success if w8 aggregate correct ≥ 887 (no more than 10 fewer than the full Alpha5 control).

proposal.success_criteria: Using the independent seed set B, the w8‑compressed model must achieve an aggregate Q.ANT correct count of at least 887 out of 1000 test predictions. Parameter count must remain ≤ 5,000. No other metric is required for gate passage.
proposal.risks: Potential stochastic variance could cause the w8 candidate to fall >10 predictions short, leading to a false negative. Limited seed count may not capture full variability. The experiment relies on software simulation; results may not transfer to physical photonic hardware.
